title: Primitive variable catalog and real-cluster examples (VPC/IAM/EKS/GKE/AKS)
content:
Purpose:
This note is a working catalog of Terraform primitive variables, recommended defaults, and concrete real-cluster examples for VPC, IAM, and cluster primitives (EKS/GKE/AKS). The goal is to standardize variable shapes, surface upgrade traps, and provide small sanity-test manifests teams can use when onboarding Private deployments (VPC/on-prem).

Scope and audience:
- Audience: infra engineers, SREs, solutions engineering, and module authors who maintain or consume private-deployments TF modules.
- Scope: primitives (vpc, subnet, route, nat/gateway), iam (roles, role-bindings, service accounts), and cluster primitives (eks/gke/aks bootstrap module inputs/outputs).
- Not in scope: provider-specific deep internals (CNI tuning, instance types). This focuses on interface contract and examples.

Principles and constraints (decisions to keep consistent):
1) Primitive modules must be small and composable — no large opinionated defaults that hide outputs users will need.
2) Variables should accept both explicit IDs and declarative objects. Eg allow vpc_id string OR vpc = { cidr = "...", tags = {...} } for new-create flows.
3) Outputs must be canonical and stable: namespaced under module outputs (vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, nat_gateways). Changing names requires deprecation cycle.
4) Backwards-compat: prefer additive variables and a compatibility shim var map for migration (see migration stanza below).
5) Minimal compute assumptions: do not assume instance sizing or node pools; expose nodepool/agentpool variables as lists/maps.

Variable catalog (recommended shapes and examples)
------------------------------------------------
1) VPC primitive (module: primitive-vpc)
- var vpc_id (string, optional)
  - Accepts: existing VPC id -> module creates no network resources.
  - Example: "vpc-0a1b2c3d"
- var vpc (map/object, optional)
  - Shape: { name = string, cidr = string, tags = map(string) }
  - Example: { name = "redwood-internal", cidr = "10.0.0.0/16", tags = {env="staging"} }
- var public_subnets (list(object), optional)
  - Shape element: { cidr = string, az = string?, name = string? }
  - Example: [{ cidr = "10.0.1.0/24", az = "us-west-2a", name = "pub-1" }, ...]
- var private_subnets (list(object), optional)
- var enable_nat (bool, default = true)
- var nat_type (string, default = "gateway", allowed: gateway|nat-gw|none)

Outputs (vpc module): vpc_id, vpc_cidr, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, nat_gateway_ids, route_table_ids

Notes: prefer explicit list ordering for subnets to ensure deterministic selection when modules pick a single AZ.

2) IAM primitive (module: primitive-iam)
- var iam_role_defs (list(object), optional)
  - Shape element: { name = string, assume_role_policy = string (json), managed_policies = list(string), inline_policies = map(string) }
  - Example: [{ name = "redwood-node-role", assume_role_policy = "...json...", managed_policies = ["arn:aws:iam::aws:policy/AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy"] }]
- var sa_bindings (list(object), optional)
  - For k8s service account -> iam mapping (useful for IRSA)
  - Shape: { namespace = string, name = string, iam_role = string }
Outputs: role_arns, role_names, service_account_id_map (map k8s->iam)

3) Cluster primitive (EKS/GKE/AKS) — module: primitive-cluster
- var cluster_id (string, optional) – accepts existing cluster id for attach-only flows.
- var cluster = object or map for create flows
  - Shape minimal: { name = string, kubernetes_version = string, network = object (ref vpc outputs), control_plane_subnets = list(string) }
- var node_pools (list(object))
  - element shape: { name = string, min = number, max = number, instance_types = list(string), labels = map(string), taints = list(object) }
  - Example: [{ name = "general", min = 2, max = 5, instance_types = ["m6i.large"], labels = { workload = "general" } }]
- var enable_oidc (bool, default = true)
- var addons (map) — for optional managed addons like aws-ebs-csi-driver; prefer map of booleans/configs

Outputs (cluster): cluster_endpoint, cluster_certificate, kubeconfig (sensitive), node_pool_ids, node_role_arn, cluster_security_group_id

Design patterns and examples (real cluster snippets)
---------------------------------------------------
Example A: New VPC + EKS cluster (minimal usable)
vars.tfvars:
vpc = { name = "customer-x-vpc", cidr = "10.10.0.0/16", tags = {owner="solutions"} }
public_subnets = [{ cidr = "10.10.1.0/24", az = "us-west-2a" }, { cidr = "10.10.2.0/24", az = "us-west-2b" }]
private_subnets = [{ cidr = "10.10.11.0/24", az = "us-west-2a" }, { cidr = "10.10.12.0/24", az = "us-west-2b" }]
enable_nat = true
cluster = { name = "redwood-stage-eks", kubernetes_version = "1.27" }
node_pools = [{ name = "workers", min = 2, max = 4, instance_types = ["m6i.large"] }]

Operation: run apply on primitive-vpc -> consume module outputs into primitive-cluster inputs. Use terraform workspace per-customer to isolate state.

Example B: Bring-your-own VPC and attach (common enterprise request)
vars.tfvars:
vpc_id = "vpc-0df12345"
cluster_id = null  # cluster will be created, but using the provided vpc
public_subnets = null  # rely on subnets passed by vpc lookup map
# module does: if vpc_id provided -> data "aws_vpc" lookup and populate subnet lists from tags or explicit subnet_ids var

Migration & upgrade patterns (practical playbook)
--------------------------------------------------
Problem: Changing variable shapes breaks downstream consumers. Example: switching from public_subnet_ids (list(string)) to public_subnets (list(object)) will break existing uses.
Recommended path:
1) Introduce new variable with _v2 suffix (public_subnets_v2) accepting the richer object. Keep old var supported.
2) Add an internal mapping step in module: if public_subnets_v2 != null -> compute public_subnet_ids from it; else use public_subnet_ids.
3) Emit a deprecation warning in module log (terraform null_resource + local-exec echo) for now.
4) At end of a deprecation period (3 months / two releases), flip default and remove old var in a major-version bump with clear migration guide.

Compatibility shim example (pseudo tf logic):
locals {
  public_subnet_source = length(var.public_subnets_v2) > 0 ? var.public_subnets_v2 : [ for id in var.public_subnet_ids : { id = id } ]
}
# downstream resources reference local.public_subnet_source[*].id

Sanity tests and tiny test manifests (what to run before merging interface changes)
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Minimal create flow: new VPC + cluster with 2 AZs, node pool scale to 0->2. Validate outputs exist and kubeconfig can authenticate.
2) Attach flow: provide vpc_id + explicit subnet ids, ensure module does not attempt to create new network resources.
3) Upgrade flow: start with old var shape, then apply module version with compatibility shim to ensure no drift.
4) Deletion safety: ensure module exports IDs and has destroy-time behavior checked in canary account.
5) IAM safety: run IAM role trust policy validation (ensure we don't grant wildcard principals).

Operational notes and gotchas
-----------------------------
- Tagging: modules should accept a tags map and apply them consistently to all created resources. Do not rely on provider default tags only.
- Cross-account considerations: always expose role_arn outputs and avoid implicit hardcodes. Provide documented step to create cross-account role binding for private deployments.
- Secrets: kubeconfig should be marked sensitive; modules should not print secrets to logs. Use provider aliasing for multi-account flows.
- AZ mapping: cloud providers may return AZs in different order — modules must sort by AZ name for deterministic behavior when selecting AZ-indexed resources.
- Drift and state: recommend using remote backend per-customer and terraform state locking. Document guidelines for import when adopting an existing cluster.

Testing and CI recommendations
-------------------------------
- Each module change that touches variable interface must run acceptance tests in a small sandbox account. Keep a curated list of smoke test manifests under infra-modules/testmanifests/ for quick runs.
- Maintain a matrix of provider versions and k8s versions for which we've validated the module. Keep this matrix in a markdown file alongside module.

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self)
------------------------------------
- Decide canonical name for kubeconfig output (kubeconfig_raw vs kubeconfig). We need to be consistent across cloud modules.
- Confirm default nat strategy for on-prem users — we currently assume managed NAT GW but some on-prem connectors expect explicit NAT instances.
- Add standardized variable for labeling resources with org/owner/id to aid billing and troubleshooting.
- Need clear guidance for GKE/AKS differences (node pool naming semantics) — next iteration will include provider-specific example blocks.

References and quick links:
- Jira: JIRA-PD-1187 (module variable standardization epic)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/452 (initial reconciliation of vpc primitives)
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-3245 (private-deployments onboarding runbook)

Appendix: short checklist for module authors before tagging release
------------------------------------------------------------------
- [ ] Add compatibility shim and tests if changing any public var/outputs
- [ ] Add example tfvars for both create and attach flows
- [ ] Ensure all outputs are documented in module README with example values
- [ ] Run acceptance smoke tests in sandbox account and record results in PR description
- [ ] Add migration notes to CHANGELOG and link to Jira ticket

End of note.
